title: Cohomology of a finite projective complex over a coherent ring
statement: Let R be a commutative coherent ring, meaning that every finitely generated ideal of R is finitely presented. Let P^\bullet be a bounded cochain complex of finite projective R-modules (the affine form of a strictly perfect complex [def-pc-perfect-complex]). Then each cohomology module H^q(P^\bullet) is finitely presented over R.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 0EWZ (over a coherent ring a pseudo-coherent complex has coherent cohomology), with Algebra, Lemma 05CX (coherent = finitely presented over a coherent ring)

proof.text: Each finite projective term P^q is finitely presented [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-finitely-presented]. Since R is coherent, [lem-sc-coherent-ring-fp-kernel-cokernel] applies to every differential d^q:P^q\to P^{q+1}, so Z^q=\operatorname{Ker}(d^q) and B^q=\operatorname{Im}(d^{q-1}) are finitely presented.

source.place: Lemmas 05CW and 05CX applied to the differentials

proof.text: The inclusion B^q\hookrightarrow Z^q is a map between finitely presented modules. Applying [lem-sc-coherent-ring-fp-kernel-cokernel] shows its cokernel is finitely presented; this cokernel is H^q(P^\bullet)=Z^q/B^q.
